name: Lios

attributes.attribute: an Irish term for an ancient site

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Lios is an Irish term for a mythological site. The name is often used to describe the hillforts and stone circles that mark the land. One site of that name is the largest stone circle in the country, with a circumference of almost 160 feet. The ring stands near the mythologically important Lough Gur and is older than the Celtic arrival in Ireland by as much as 4,000 years. Like many such structures it is set to the path of the sky, in this case turned toward the moon as it goes down at midsummer.

okr.objective: Describe Lios as the source names it among Irish sites.
